items.response: Good call on not saying anything to Grace, and sorry Sam's had a rough afternoon. For Grace and Daniel, keep it unscented and local: something edible like a nice jar of maple syrup or honey, a book for Daniel (he's a retired civil engineer, so local history or bridges would suit), and for Grace, who still teaches piano, a piano-themed book or sheet music collection. I'd skip flowers too, since lilies and the like can be strong. Action: I'll look up a few open-tomorrow shops near Alta Vista, check their hours before sending you a shortlist, and hold off buying anything until you pick.

For Tom's calendar, the things I can see are: Thu 10 Dec early leave at 5:00 pm for Leo's winter concert (you already told Tom, so it just needs to be on the calendar), and your Lisbon trip, where you fly Sun 20 Dec at 22:10 and return Sat 2 Jan, so you'd be out Mon 21 Dec through Fri 1 Jan, plus possibly an early leave on the 20th to get to Pearson. I'm not sure about Fri 18 Dec (Leo's last school day) or any company holidays, so I'll ask rather than guess. I don't have a record of the school-closure thing from last winter, so I'd rather not guess; any detail you remember (snow day? what Leo was doing?) helps, and I can search photos and messages from that week. Action: I'll draft the calendar entries for 10 Dec and 21 Dec to 1 Jan as tentative, ask you about the 18th and the 20th, and search your photos and chats from last winter for the school-closure day.

Action: I'll pull the office address from your calendar, look for places within a short walk with space for 8 next Thursday, and send you a shortlist with menus, though it would help to know any dietary needs and a rough budget per head.

Sounds good, I'll take it from here and book without checking in. I don't have a card or loyalty account on file for hotels, so if there's no default payment method I'll have to ask you for that one thing. Added to the recap as an action item with you as owner. I don't know opening hours or what the lavender farm is doing on that date, so I'll check those instead of guessing. Happy to. Leo was born July 17, 2019, so he's a child applicant under 16, and the checklist is roughly: the child passport application form, two passport photos (your open to-do from October is still to get these for Leo), proof of citizenship such as his birth certificate, his current passport, a parent or guardian's ID, and the fee. I'll confirm the exact current requirements, fees and processing times on the official site instead of quoting from memory, since his passport expires in January and timing matters. Action: I'll build the checklist from the government site, find the nearest Service Canada or passport office with appointment availability, and send you the options.

Happy to help find one. I don't have notes on which language you're studying or your level beyond what you said, so I won't guess the language. Action: tell me the language, and I'll shortlist two or three upper-intermediate grammar books that have exercises and an answer key, with prices, and check with you before ordering anything.

Happy long weekend! Here's the order I'd do it in: 1) find the good extension cord first, since it helps with the rest; 2) sort the garage recycling; 3) fix Leo's bike chain; 4) hang the hallway mirror (about 15 kg on plaster and lath, so use two #10 x 3 in screws into a stud, or two 1/4 in snap toggles or a 60 cm French cleat, and tape the spot first); 5) plant the tomato seedlings last, in the cooler part of the day. For the mirror, the hardware list was snap toggles ($9.49), a French cleat kit ($24.99) and painter's tape ($6.99) from Home Hardware on Queen St E, so check you have those before starting. Action: I'll save this as a checklist, and I'll check whether Home Hardware is open today if you need anything.
